155	        provider_name: Option<&str>,
156	        usage: ProviderUsage,
157	    ) -> Result<SpendEstimate> {
158	        let route = provider_name
159	            .and_then(|name| self.routes.iter().find(|route| route.name() == name))
160	            .or_else(|| self.routes.first())
161	            .ok_or_else(|| ProviderError::NoRoute("empty provider route".to_string()))?;
162	        Ok(route.estimate_spend(usage))
163	    }
164	}
165	
166	fn configured_route_names(
167	    default_provider: Option<String>,
168	    fallback: Option<Vec<String>>,
169	) -> Vec<String> {
170	    let mut route_names = Vec::new();
171	    if let Some(default_provider) = default_provider {
172	        route_names.push(default_provider);
173	    }
174	    if let Some(fallback) = fallback {
175	        for provider in fallback {
176	            if !route_names.iter().any(|route| route == &provider) {
177	                route_names.push(provider);
178	            }
179	        }
180	    }
181	    if route_names.is_empty() {
182	        route_names.extend([
183	            "cli:claude-code".to_string(),
184	            "cli:codex".to_string(),
185	            "anthropic".to_string(),
186	            "openai".to_string(),
187	            "openai-compatible".to_string(),
188	        ]);
189	    }
190	    route_names
191	}
192	
193	fn build_provider(
194	    name: String,
195	    kind: ProviderKind,
196	    entry: ProviderEntry,
197	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
198	) -> Result<Box<dyn Provider>> {
199	    match kind {
200	        ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode => Ok(Box::new(CliClaudeCodeProvider::new(name, entry))),
201	        ProviderKind::CliCodex => Ok(Box::new(CliCodexProvider::new(name, entry))),
202	        ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke => Ok(Box::new(ScriptedSmokeProvider::new())),
203	        ProviderKind::Anthropic | ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
204	            Ok(Box::new(ProviderAdapter::new(name, kind, entry)))
205	        }
206	        ProviderKind::Generic(id) => {
207	            let descriptor = registry
208	                .get(&id)
209	                .or_else(|| registry.get(&name))
210	                .ok_or_else(|| {
211	                    ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("generic provider {id} has no descriptor"))
212	                })?;
213	            if descriptor.kind != DescriptorKind::Cli {
214	                return Err(ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
215	                    "generic provider {id} is not a cli descriptor"
216	                )));
217	            }
218	            Ok(Box::new(GenericCliProvider::new(
219	                name,
220	                entry,
221	                descriptor.clone(),
222	            )?))
223	        }
224	    }
225	}

125	pub fn validate_acceptance_marker(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<AcceptanceMarker> {
126	    // AS-BUILT §8/§17: completion is accepted only from an external marker
127	    // written by a binary runner and bound to this run_id.
128	    let path = marker_path(state);
129	    let raw = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
130	    let marker: AcceptanceMarker = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
131	    if marker.schema_version != 1 {
132	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
133	            "unsupported acceptance marker schema {}",
134	            marker.schema_version
135	        )));
136	    }
137	    if marker.run_id != state.run_id {
138	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
139	            "acceptance marker run_id {} does not match {}",
140	            marker.run_id, state.run_id
141	        )));
142	    }
143	    if marker.status != "pass" || marker.produced_by != "dr-gate" {
144	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
145	            "acceptance marker was not produced by dr-gate with pass status".to_string(),
146	        ));
147	    }
148	    let expected = marker_signature(&state.run_root, &marker)?;
149	    if marker.signature != expected {
150	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
151	            "acceptance marker signature is invalid; forged self-attestation refused".to_string(),
152	        ));
153	    }
154	    Ok(marker)
155	}

309	fn evaluate_acceptance_checks_inner(
310	    run_root: &Path,
311	    working_dir: &Path,
312	    progress_path: Option<&Path>,
313	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
314	    let spec_path = acceptance_spec_path_for_run_root(run_root);
315	    if !spec_path.exists() {
316	        return evaluate_default_acceptance_with_progress(working_dir, progress_path);
317	    }
318	    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(&spec_path).with_path(&spec_path)?;
319	    let checks = parse_acceptance_checks(&raw)?;
320	    let total = checks.len();
321	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "started", 0, total, None)?;
322	    let mut results = Vec::new();
323	    for (idx, check) in checks.into_iter().enumerate() {
324	        let index = idx + 1;
325	        emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "running", index, total, None)?;
326	        let result = evaluate_check(working_dir, check)?;
327	        let status = if result.passed { "passed" } else { "failed" };
328	        emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, index, total, Some(result.clone()))?;
329	        results.push(result);
330	    }
331	    let status = if results
332	        .iter()
333	        .any(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
334	    {
335	        "failed"
336	    } else {
337	        "passed"
338	    };
339	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, total, total, None)?;
340	    Ok(results)
341	}
342	
343	fn evaluate_default_acceptance_with_progress(
344	    working_dir: &Path,
345	    progress_path: Option<&Path>,
346	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
347	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "started", 0, 1, None)?;
348	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, "running", 1, 1, None)?;
349	    let results = evaluate_default_acceptance(working_dir)?;
350	    if let Some(result) = results.first().cloned() {
351	        let status = if result.passed { "passed" } else { "failed" };
352	        emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, 1, 1, Some(result))?;
353	    }
354	    let status = if results
355	        .iter()
356	        .any(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
357	    {
358	        "failed"
359	    } else {
360	        "passed"
361	    };
362	    emit_acceptance_progress(progress_path, status, 1, 1, None)?;
363	    Ok(results)
364	}

366	fn emit_acceptance_progress(
367	    progress_path: Option<&Path>,
368	    status: &str,

379	            checked_at: Utc::now(),
380	            status: status.to_string(),
381	            index,
382	            total,
383	            result,
384	        },
385	    )
386	}
387	
388	fn evaluate_default_acceptance(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
389	    if working_dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
390	        let started = Instant::now();
391	        let output = Command::new("cargo")
392	            .arg("test")
393	            .current_dir(working_dir)
394	            .output()
395	            .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
396	                path: working_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
397	                source,
398	            })?;
399	        return Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
400	            kind: "cargo_test".to_string(),
401	            passed: output.status.success(),
402	            must_pass: true,
403	            detail: format!("cargo test exited with {}", output.status),
404	            command: Some("cargo test".to_string()),
405	            cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
406	            duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
407	            stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
408	            stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
409	        }]);
410	    }
411	    if !working_dir.is_dir() {
412	        return Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
413	            kind: "working_dir".to_string(),
414	            passed: false,
415	            must_pass: true,
416	            detail: format!("working directory missing: {}", working_dir.display()),
417	            command: None,
418	            cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
419	            duration_ms: None,
420	            stdout: None,
421	            stderr: None,
422	        }]);
423	    }
424	    Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
425	        kind: "working_dir".to_string(),
426	        passed: true,
427	        must_pass: true,
428	        detail: "working directory exists".to_string(),
429	        command: None,
430	        cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
431	        duration_ms: None,
432	        stdout: None,
433	        stderr: None,
434	    }])
435	}
436	
437	fn evaluate_check(working_dir: &Path, check: AcceptanceCheck) -> Result<AcceptanceCheckResult> {
438	    match check {
439	        AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest { args, must_pass } => {
440	            let started = Instant::now();
441	            let output = Command::new("cargo")
442	                .arg("test")
443	                .args(&args)
444	                .current_dir(working_dir)
445	                .output()
446	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
447	                    path: working_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
448	                    source,
449	                })?;
450	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
451	                kind: "cargo_test".to_string(),
452	                passed: output.status.success(),
453	                must_pass,
454	                detail: format!("cargo test exited with {}", output.status),
455	                command: Some(format_command("cargo test", &args)),
456	                cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
457	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
458	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
459	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
460	            })
461	        }
462	        AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { path, must_pass } => {
463	            let path = render_template(working_dir, &path);
464	            let exists = path.exists();
465	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
466	                kind: "file_exists".to_string(),
467	                passed: exists,
468	                must_pass,
469	                detail: if exists {
470	                    format!("{} exists", path.display())
471	                } else {
472	                    format!("{} is missing", path.display())
473	                },
474	                command: None,
475	                cwd: None,
476	                duration_ms: None,
477	                stdout: None,
478	                stderr: None,
479	            })
480	        }
481	        AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch {
482	            path,
483	            pattern,
484	            must_pass,
485	        } => {
486	            let path = render_template(working_dir, &path);
487	            let body = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
488	            let matched = regex::Regex::new(&pattern)
489	                .map(|regex| regex.is_match(&body))
490	                .unwrap_or_else(|_| body.contains(&pattern));
491	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
492	                kind: "content_match".to_string(),
493	                passed: matched,
494	                must_pass,
495	                detail: if matched {
496	                    format!("{} matches {:?}", path.display(), pattern)
497	                } else {
498	                    format!("{} does not match {:?}", path.display(), pattern)
499	                },
500	                command: None,
501	                cwd: None,
502	                duration_ms: None,
503	                stdout: None,
504	                stderr: None,
505	            })
506	        }
507	        AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { cwd, must_pass } => {
508	            let cwd = render_template(working_dir, &cwd);
509	            let started = Instant::now();
510	            let output = Command::new("cargo")
511	                .arg("build")
512	                .current_dir(&cwd)
513	                .output()
514	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
515	                    path: cwd.join("Cargo.toml"),
516	                    source,
517	                })?;
518	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
519	                kind: "build_success".to_string(),
520	                passed: output.status.success(),
521	                must_pass,
522	                detail: format!(
523	                    "cargo build in {} exited with {}",
524	                    cwd.display(),
525	                    output.status
526	                ),
527	                command: Some("cargo build".to_string()),
528	                cwd: Some(cwd),
529	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
530	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
531	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
532	            })
533	        }
534	        AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
535	            command,
536	            cwd,
537	            must_pass,
538	        } => {
539	            let cwd = cwd
540	                .map(|cwd| render_template(working_dir, &cwd))
541	                .unwrap_or_else(|| working_dir.to_path_buf());
542	            let started = Instant::now();
543	            let output = Command::new("sh")
544	                .arg("-lc")
545	                .arg(&command)
546	                .current_dir(&cwd)
547	                .output()
548	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
549	                    path: cwd.clone(),
550	                    source,
551	                })?;
552	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
553	                kind: "shell".to_string(),
554	                passed: output.status.success(),
555	                must_pass,
556	                detail: format!(
557	                    "shell {:?} in {} exited with {}",
558	                    command,
559	                    cwd.display(),
560	                    output.status
561	                ),
562	                command: Some(command),
563	                cwd: Some(cwd),
564	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
565	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
566	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
567	            })
568	        }
569	    }
570	}
571	
572	fn duration_ms(started: Instant) -> u64 {
573	    started.elapsed().as_millis().min(u128::from(u64::MAX)) as u64
574	}
575	
576	fn clipped_stdout(output: &Output) -> Option<String> {
577	    clipped_output(&output.stdout)
578	}
579	
580	fn clipped_stderr(output: &Output) -> Option<String> {
581	    clipped_output(&output.stderr)
582	}
583	
584	fn clipped_output(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
585	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).trim().to_string();
586	    if text.is_empty() {
587	        None
588	    } else {
589	        Some(clip_text(&text, 4096))
590	    }
591	}
592	
593	fn clip_text(text: &str, limit: usize) -> String {
594	    if text.len() <= limit {
595	        return text.to_string();
596	    }
597	    let mut clipped = text
598	        .char_indices()
599	        .take_while(|(idx, _)| *idx < limit)
600	        .map(|(_, ch)| ch)
601	        .collect::<String>();
602	    clipped.push_str("\n... output truncated ...");
603	    clipped
604	}
605	
606	fn format_command(base: &str, args: &[String]) -> String {
607	    if args.is_empty() {
608	        base.to_string()
609	    } else {
610	        format!("{base} {}", args.join(" "))
611	    }
612	}
613	
614	fn parse_acceptance_checks(raw: &str) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheck>> {
615	    let root: YamlValue = serde_yaml::from_str(raw).map_err(|source| {
616	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("invalid acceptance.yaml: {source}"))
617	    })?;
618	    let mut checks = Vec::new();
619	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "checks")) {
620	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item, None)?);
621	    }
622	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "required")) {
623	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item, Some(true))?);
624	    }
625	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "optional")) {
626	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item, Some(false))?);
627	    }
628	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "tests")) {
629	        checks.push(parse_shell_check(item, true)?);
630	    }
631	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "file-exists")) {
632	        checks.push(parse_file_exists_check(item, true)?);
633	    }
634	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "content-match")) {
635	        checks.push(parse_content_match_check(item, true)?);
636	    }
637	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "build-success")) {
638	        checks.push(parse_build_success_check(item, true));
639	    }
640	    Ok(checks)
641	}
642	
643	fn parse_check_value(value: &YamlValue, force_must_pass: Option<bool>) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
644	    if let Ok(mut check) = serde_yaml::from_value::<AcceptanceCheck>(value.clone()) {
645	        if let Some(must_pass) = force_must_pass {
646	            check.set_must_pass(must_pass);
647	        }
648	        return Ok(check);
649	    }
650	    if let Some(command) = yaml_string(value) {
651	        return Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
652	            command,
653	            cwd: None,
654	            must_pass: force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true),
655	        });
656	    }
657	    let Some((kind, body)) = single_key_mapping(value) else {
658	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
659	            "invalid acceptance check: {:?}",
660	            value
661	        )));
662	    };
663	    let must_pass = force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true);
664	    match kind.as_str() {
665	        "file-exists" | "file_exists" => parse_file_exists_check(body, must_pass),
666	        "content-match" | "content_match" => parse_content_match_check(body, must_pass),
667	        "build-success" | "build_success" => Ok(parse_build_success_check(body, must_pass)),
668	        "shell" | "test" => parse_shell_check(body, must_pass),
669	        "cargo-test" | "cargo_test" => Ok(AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest {
670	            args: yaml_string(body).map(|arg| vec![arg]).unwrap_or_default(),
671	            must_pass,
672	        }),
673	        other => Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
674	            "unknown acceptance check kind {other}"
675	        ))),
676	    }
677	}
678	
679	fn parse_file_exists_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
680	    let path = yaml_string(value)
681	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(value, "path").and_then(yaml_string))
682	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("file-exists requires path".to_string()))?;
683	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { path, must_pass })
684	}
685	
686	fn parse_content_match_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
687	    let path = yaml_get(value, "path")
688	        .and_then(yaml_string)
689	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires path".to_string()))?;
690	    let pattern = yaml_get(value, "pattern")
691	        .and_then(yaml_string)
692	        .ok_or_else(|| {
693	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires pattern".to_string())
694	        })?;
695	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch {
696	        path,
697	        pattern,
698	        must_pass,
699	    })
700	}
701	
702	fn parse_build_success_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> AcceptanceCheck {
703	    let cwd = yaml_string(value)
704	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string))
705	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "{working_dir}".to_string());
706	    AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { cwd, must_pass }
707	}
708	
709	fn parse_shell_check(value: &YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
710	    let command = yaml_string(value)
711	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(value, "command").and_then(yaml_string))
712	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("shell check requires command".to_string()))?;
713	    let cwd = yaml_get(value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string);
714	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
715	        command,
716	        cwd,
717	        must_pass,
718	    })
719	}
720	
721	fn yaml_get<'a>(value: &'a YamlValue, key: &str) -> Option<&'a YamlValue> {
722	    value.as_mapping()?.get(YamlValue::String(key.to_string()))
723	}
724	
725	fn yaml_seq(value: Option<&YamlValue>) -> Vec<&YamlValue> {
726	    match value {
727	        Some(YamlValue::Sequence(values)) => values.iter().collect(),
728	        Some(value) => vec![value],
729	        None => Vec::new(),
730	    }
731	}
732	
733	fn yaml_string(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<String> {
734	    value.as_str().map(ToString::to_string)
735	}
736	
737	fn single_key_mapping(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<(String, &YamlValue)> {
738	    let mapping = value.as_mapping()?;
739	    if mapping.len() != 1 {
740	        return None;
741	    }
742	    let (key, value) = mapping.iter().next()?;
743	    Some((key.as_str()?.to_string(), value))
744	}
745	
746	impl AcceptanceCheck {
747	    fn set_must_pass(&mut self, value: bool) {
748	        match self {
749	            AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest { must_pass, .. }
750	            | AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { must_pass, .. }
751	            | AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch { must_pass, .. }
752	            | AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { must_pass, .. }
753	            | AcceptanceCheck::Shell { must_pass, .. } => *must_pass = value,
754	        }
755	    }
756	}
757	
758	fn render_template(working_dir: &Path, value: &str) -> PathBuf {
759	    PathBuf::from(value.replace("{working_dir}", &working_dir.to_string_lossy()))
760	}
761	
762	fn marker_signature(run_root: &Path, marker: &AcceptanceMarker) -> Result<String> {
763	    let nonce_path = gate_nonce_path_for_run_root(run_root);
764	    let nonce = std::fs::read_to_string(&nonce_path).with_path(&nonce_path)?;
765	    let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
766	    nonce.trim().hash(&mut hasher);
767	    marker.schema_version.hash(&mut hasher);
768	    marker.run_id.hash(&mut hasher);
769	    marker.status.hash(&mut hasher);
770	    marker.produced_by.hash(&mut hasher);
771	    marker.checked_at.to_rfc3339().hash(&mut hasher);
772	    marker.working_dir.hash(&mut hasher);
773	    marker.check_count.hash(&mut hasher);
774	    for check in &marker.checks {
775	        check.hash(&mut hasher);
776	    }
777	    let tamper_path = crate::tamper::acceptance_tamper_path_for_run_root(run_root);
778	    match std::fs::read(&tamper_path) {
779	        Ok(bytes) => bytes.hash(&mut hasher),
780	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => "".hash(&mut hasher),
781	        Err(source) => {
782	            return Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
783	                path: tamper_path,
784	                source,
785	            });
786	        }
787	    }
788	    // A campaign result run carries its gate-verdict roll-up; binding it here means
789	    // the roll-up cannot be edited after signing to launder a refused leaf into a
790	    // clean pass. Absent (the normal, non-campaign case) hashes empty.
791	    let rollup_path = crate::campaign::rollup_path_at_run_root(run_root);
792	    match std::fs::read(&rollup_path) {
793	        Ok(bytes) => bytes.hash(&mut hasher),
794	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => "".hash(&mut hasher),
795	        Err(source) => {
796	            return Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
797	                path: rollup_path,
798	                source,
799	            });
800	        }
801	    }
802	    Ok(format!("{:016x}", hasher.finish()))
803	}
804	
805	fn default_must_pass() -> bool {
806	    true
807	}

70	impl RunEventBus {
71	    pub fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self {
72	        let (sender, _) = broadcast::channel(capacity);
73	        Self { sender }
74	    }
75	
76	    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<RunEvent> {
77	        self.sender.subscribe()
78	    }
79	
80	    pub fn emit(&self, state: &PipelineState, event: RunEventKind) -> Result<()> {
81	        emit_event(state, Some(&self.sender), event)
82	    }
83	
84	    pub fn sender(&self) -> broadcast::Sender<RunEvent> {
85	        self.sender.clone()
86	    }
87	}
88	
89	pub fn emit_event(
90	    state: &PipelineState,
91	    sender: Option<&broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
92	    event: RunEventKind,
93	) -> Result<()> {
94	    let event = RunEvent {
95	        timestamp: Utc::now(),
96	        run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
97	        event,
98	    };
99	    append_json_line(&state.run_root.join(RUN_EVENTS_JSONL), &event)?;
100	    if let Some(sender) = sender {
101	        let _ = sender.send(event);
102	    }
103	    Ok(())
104	}
105	
106	pub fn event_preview(value: impl AsRef<str>) -> String {
107	    let value = value.as_ref().replace('\n', " ");
108	    const MAX: usize = 160;
109	    if value.len() <= MAX {
110	        value
111	    } else {
112	        format!("{}...", &value[..MAX])
113	    }
114	}
115

9	fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
10	    let mut run_id = None;
11	    let mut run_root = None;
12	    let mut working_dir = None;
13	    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
14	    while let Some(arg) = args.next() {
15	        match arg.as_str() {
16	            "--run" => run_id = args.next(),
17	            "--run-root" => run_root = args.next().map(PathBuf::from),
18	            "--working-dir" => working_dir = args.next().map(PathBuf::from),
19	            other => return Err(format!("unknown argument {other}").into()),
20	        }
21	    }
22	    let run_id = run_id.ok_or("--run is required")?;
23	    let working_dir = working_dir.ok_or("--working-dir is required")?;
24	    let run_root = match run_root {
25	        Some(run_root) => run_root,
26	        None => infer_run_root(&working_dir)?,
27	    };
28	    let results = evaluate_acceptance_checks_with_progress(&run_root, &working_dir)?;
29	    let checks = compiled_acceptance_checks(&run_root, &working_dir)?;
30	    let tamper = tamper::evaluate(&run_id, &run_root, &working_dir, &checks)?;
31	    tamper::write_acceptance_tamper(&run_root, &tamper)?;
32	    if tamper.verdict == AcceptanceTamperVerdict::Refuse {
33	        eprintln!("acceptance refused");
34	        for reason in &tamper.refusal_reasons {
35	            eprintln!("refuse: {reason}");
36	        }
37	        return Err(format!("acceptance refused: {}", tamper.refusal_reasons.join("; ")).into());
38	    }
39	    if let Some(failed) = results
40	        .iter()
41	        .find(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
42	    {
43	        eprintln!("acceptance failed");
44	        for result in &results {
45	            let mark = if result.passed { "PASS" } else { "FAIL" };
46	            let required = if result.must_pass {
47	                "required"
48	            } else {
49	                "optional"
50	            };
51	            eprintln!("{mark} {required} {}: {}", result.kind, result.detail);
52	            if !result.passed {
53	                if let Some(stderr) = result.stderr.as_deref() {
54	                    eprintln!("stderr: {}", one_line(stderr, 500));
55	                }
56	                if let Some(stdout) = result.stdout.as_deref() {
57	                    eprintln!("stdout: {}", one_line(stdout, 500));
58	                }
59	            }
60	        }
61	        return Err(format!("required check failed: {}", failed.detail).into());
62	    }
63	    write_acceptance_marker_with_results(&run_root, run_id, working_dir, results)?;
64	    Ok(())
65	}
66	
67	fn one_line(value: &str, limit: usize) -> String {
68	    let compact = value.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
69	    if compact.len() <= limit {
70	        compact
71	    } else {
72	        let clipped = compact.chars().take(limit).collect::<String>();
73	        format!("{clipped}...")
74	    }
75	}
76	
77	fn infer_run_root(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
78	    if working_dir.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) != Some("working") {
79	        return Err("working directory must be <run-root>/working".into());
80	    }
81	    working_dir
82	        .parent()
83	        .map(Path::to_path_buf)
84	        .ok_or_else(|| "working directory has no parent".into())
85	}

46	    pub(crate) async fn refresh(&mut self, wait: Duration) -> std::io::Result<Vec<RunEvent>> {
47	        let mut events = Vec::new();
48	        match &mut self.source {
49	            TuiEventSource::Broadcast { receiver, replay } => {
50	                drain_receiver(receiver, &mut events);
51	                if events.is_empty() && !wait.is_zero() {
52	                    match tokio::time::timeout(wait, receiver.recv()).await {
53	                        Ok(Ok(event)) => events.push(event),
54	                        Ok(Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)))
55	                        | Ok(Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed)) => {
56	                            events.extend(replay.read_new()?);
57	                        }
58	                        Err(_) => {}
59	                    }
60	                }
61	                drain_receiver(receiver, &mut events);
62	                if events.is_empty() {
63	                    events.extend(replay.read_new()?);
64	                } else {
65	                    replay.skip_to_end();
66	                }
67	            }
68	            TuiEventSource::FileTail(replay) => {
69	                events.extend(replay.read_new()?);
70	            }
71	        }

81	fn drain_receiver(receiver: &mut broadcast::Receiver<RunEvent>, events: &mut Vec<RunEvent>) {
82	    loop {

84	            Ok(event) => events.push(event),
85	            Err(broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Lagged(_)) => continue,
86	            Err(broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Empty)
87	            | Err(broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Closed) => break,
88	        }

1	# deadreckon — Tamper-Evident Gate Rider (close the hollow pass)
2	
3	This rider holds the prescriptive constraints for the goal at
4	`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-28-1556-deadreckon-tamper-evident-gate-goal.md`.
5	It supersedes nothing in prior riders (notably
6	`2026-05-11-2110-deadreckon-audit-harden-rider.md`,
7	`2026-05-26-1546-deadreckon-narrative-attach-rider.md`) — their invariants still
8	apply. This rider adds **tamper-evidence**: the gate refuses to sign, or signs
9	with a surfaced caveat, when a run modified the acceptance contract itself or a
10	file an acceptance check covers; and it surfaces per-check verdicts plus honest
11	subscription spend on every result surface.
12	
13	**All paths absolute.** Source `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`, runtime `~/.deadreckon/`.
14	
15	## The bug this closes (read before designing)
16	
17	`dr-gate` (`crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs`) calls
18	`evaluate_acceptance_checks_with_progress(run_root, working_dir)` then
19	`write_acceptance_marker_with_results(...)`. The marker signature already binds
20	the check *results* (`gate.rs::marker_signature` hashes every
21	`AcceptanceCheckResult`), so a *post-hoc edit of the marker* is caught
22	(`marker_signature_includes_check_results`). The unclosed hole is upstream: the
23	agent can make the checks **honestly pass** by changing what they check.
24	
25	- Default acceptance is "`cargo test` passes" when `Cargo.toml` exists
26	  (`gate.rs::evaluate_default_acceptance`). An agent that **deletes the failing
27	  test** gets a green `cargo test` and a valid signature.
28	- A `shell` check compiled as `pytest || true` (or `--no-verify`, `--exit-zero`)
29	  exits 0 forever; `evaluate_check` reports `passed: output.status.success()`.
30	- A `content_match`/`file_exists` check can be satisfied by the agent writing the
31	  literal matched string into the very file under inspection.
32	
33	The signature is real; the exam was rigged. We make the rigging **visible**
34	(tamper-evidence) and **refuse** the unambiguous cases. This is heuristic, not a
35	soundness proof — say so in the docs.
36	
37	## Posture (decided — do not redesign)
38	
39	- **Production-release track.** Release-blocking gate behavior. Not provisional.
40	- **Files-not-fields.** The tamper verdict is a new file
41	  `<run-root>/proofs/acceptance-tamper.json`. **No** new `PipelineState`, `Plan`,
42	  `AcceptanceMarker`, `AcceptanceCheckResult`, or provider-config fields. The
43	  marker stays `schema_version: 1`; its signature gains the tamper-file digest as
44	  an *external hashed input* (mirrors `PromotionManifest.provenance_hash`), which
45	  needs no marker field.
46	- **Tamper-evidence, not tamper-proof.** Refuse only unambiguous cases; downgrade
47	  ambiguous ones to a surfaced caveat; never silently pass a tampered run.
48	- **Reuse the non-terminal gate-failure path.** A refusal writes no marker, so the
49	  existing turn-loop behavior (gate fails -> loop continues with a corrective
50	  reason -> turn budget bounds it) applies unchanged. Do not invent a new
51	  terminal state.
52	- **No `git push`.** Phased local commits only.
53	- **No V1 invention.** Larger designs (causal tamper proofs, language-aware test
54	  detection, signed audit log) go to `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
55	- **Edits stay inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`.**
56	
57	## Data model (files, not fields)
58	
59	New file `<run-root>/proofs/acceptance-tamper.json`:
60	
61	```jsonc
62	{
63	  "schema_version": 1,
64	  "run_id": "…",
65	  "evaluated_at": "RFC3339",
66	  "verdict": "clean" | "caveat" | "refuse",
67	  "spec_modified": false,             // acceptance.yaml touched this run
68	  "lint_findings": [                  // suppression patterns in compiled checks
69	    { "check_kind": "shell", "command": "pytest || true", "pattern": "|| true" }
70	  ],
71	  "covered_files_touched": [          // check-covered files modified/deleted this run
72	    { "path": "tests/auth_test.rs", "change": "deleted",  "by_check": "cargo_test", "classification": "test" },
73	    { "path": "README.md",          "change": "modified", "by_check": "file_exists", "classification": "target" }
74	  ],
75	  "caveats": [ "agent modified test file tests/auth_test.rs this run" ],
76	  "refusal_reasons": [ ]             // non-empty iff verdict == "refuse"
77	}
78	```
79	
80	`change` ∈ `modified | deleted | created`. `classification` ∈
81	`test | target | build | unknown` (see coverage rules). `clean` =>
82	`covered_files_touched`, `caveats`, `lint_findings`, `refusal_reasons` all empty
83	and `spec_modified` false.
84	
85	## Detection (the spec — match it in code)
86	
87	Put the new logic in a dedicated core module
88	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/tamper.rs` (re-exported from `lib.rs`); keep
89	`gate.rs` and `dr-gate.rs` thin callers. Pure functions, unit-testable without a
90	provider or sandbox.
91	
92	### Touched-file set
93	
94	`touched_files(run_root, working_dir) -> BTreeMap<RelPath, Change>`:
95	
96	- **Modified/created**: union of every `files` entry across `provenance.jsonl`
97	  (`ProvenanceRecord.files`), normalized to working-dir-relative paths
98	  (strip the `working_dir` prefix; ignore paths outside it).
99	- **Deleted**: diff the **earliest** snapshot inventory
100	  (`<run-root>/snapshots/turn-*` lowest N, via `inventory_files`) against the
101	  final `working_dir` inventory. A path present in the first snapshot and absent
102	  now is `deleted`. (Provenance does not reliably record deletions; the snapshot
103	  diff is what catches the deleted-test attack.)
104	- Always exclude the `.deadreckon/` subtree (run-owned docs/state), so generated
105	  `RUN-*.md` never counts as tampering.
106	
107	### Check coverage
108	
109	`check_coverage(checks, working_dir) -> Vec<CheckCoverage>` maps each
110	`AcceptanceCheck` to the working-dir-relative paths it depends on and a
111	`classification`:
112	
113	- `FileExists { path }` / `ContentMatch { path }` -> exact rendered path
114	  (`render_template`); `classification = target`.
115	- `BuildSuccess { cwd }` -> the `cwd` directory; `classification = build`
116	  (low signal — included for completeness, never by itself a caveat).
117	- `CargoTest { .. }` (and the default `cargo test`) -> test files under
118	  `working_dir`: paths matching `**/tests/**/*.rs`, `*_test.rs`, or any `.rs`
119	  file whose contents contain `#[test]` or `#[cfg(test)]`;
120	  `classification = test`.
121	- `Shell { command, .. }` -> (a) **lint** the command string for suppression
122	  patterns; (b) best-effort path extraction: whitespace tokens that resolve to an
123	  existing working-dir path; test-name heuristic above sets `test`, else
124	  `unknown`. Path extraction is best-effort; the lint is authoritative.
125	
126	### Suppression-pattern lint
127	
128	`lint_suppressions(command) -> Vec<Finding>` flags (case-insensitive, token-aware
129	so `||true` and `|| true` both hit): `|| true`, `; true`, `&& true`, `| true`,
130	`|| exit 0`, `--no-verify`, `--exit-zero`, `|| :`. Applies to `Shell.command`
131	and any `CargoTest`/`BuildSuccess` extra args. Used at **two** sites: def-done
132	compile time (P4, reject) and gate time for legacy/edited specs (P5, refuse).
133	
134	### Verdict policy
135	
136	`classify(spec_modified, lint_findings, covered_touched) -> Verdict`:
137	
138	1. **refuse** iff `spec_modified` OR `!lint_findings.is_empty()`.
139	2. else **caveat** iff any `covered_files_touched` has `classification ∈
140	   {test, target}` (i.e. the agent changed a *test* or the *literal artifact a
141	   check inspects*). `build`/`unknown`-only touches do **not** trigger a caveat
142	   but are still recorded.
143	3. else **clean**.
144	
145	Rationale to preserve in code comments: modifying *production* code that a test
146	*exercises* is the whole point of a run and must stay `clean`; the danger is
147	editing the test/assertion or the contract. The heuristic intentionally errs
148	toward a visible caveat over a silent pass, and toward refuse only when the
149	contract itself or a check's exit code was subverted.
150	
151	## Gate integration (P5)
152	
153	`dr-gate.rs`, after `evaluate_acceptance_checks_with_progress` and before
154	writing the marker:
155	
156	```
157	let tamper = tamper::evaluate(&run_root, &working_dir, &compiled_checks)?;
158	write tamper -> proofs/acceptance-tamper.json   // always, all three verdicts
159	match tamper.verdict {
160	    Refuse  => { print refusal_reasons to stderr; exit nonzero; NO marker }
161	    Caveat  => { write_acceptance_marker_with_results(...) }  // signed, caveat on file
162	    Clean   => { write_acceptance_marker_with_results(...) }  // unchanged path
163	}
164	```

166	`gate.rs::marker_signature` gains the tamper-file digest as a hashed input:
167	read `proofs/acceptance-tamper.json` bytes (empty string if absent, for
168	backward tolerance) and `.hash()` them alongside the existing fields. Therefore
169	`validate_acceptance_marker` (already the promotion guard) transitively rejects
170	any marker whose tamper file was altered after signing — the agent cannot edit
171	`acceptance-tamper.json` to erase a caveat without invalidating the signature,
172	and cannot fabricate a Clean tamper file to accompany a marker it cannot sign.
173	
174	`compiled_checks` must be the same parsed `Vec<AcceptanceCheck>` the evaluator
175	used (factor a `parse for run_root` helper out of `evaluate_acceptance_checks_inner`

2237	## 35. Tamper-Evident Gate
2238	
2239	### 35.1 The hollow-pass attack
2240	
2241	The original gate signature proved that `dr-gate` wrote a marker for the check results it observed. It did not prove the checks were still meaningful. A run could delete a failing Rust test before default `cargo test`, edit the done-criteria file, or turn a shell check into `pytest || true`; the resulting checks would honestly pass and the marker signature would remain valid. The tamper-evident gate closes that release-blocking gap by refusing unambiguous contract subversion and surfacing ambiguous check-covered edits as caveats.
2242	
2243	### 35.2 Touched-file set
2244	
2245	`tamper::touched_files(run_root, working_dir)` uses two inputs. Modified and created files come from the union of `ProvenanceRecord.files` in `provenance.jsonl`, normalized relative to the run working directory. Deleted files come from the earliest `snapshots/turn-*` inventory diffed against the final working tree, because provenance rows do not reliably record deletions. The `.deadreckon/` subtree is ignored so run-owned docs and helper state do not count as tampering.
2246	
2247	### 35.3 Check coverage and classification
2248	
2249	`tamper::check_coverage` maps compiled `AcceptanceCheck` values to working-tree-relative paths:
2250	
2251	- `file_exists` and `content_match` cover their rendered target path with `target` classification.
2252	- `build_success` covers its rendered cwd as `build`, which is recorded but does not trigger a caveat by itself.
2253	- `cargo_test` covers Rust test files under `tests/`, `*_test.rs`, and `.rs` files containing `#[test]` or `#[cfg(test)]`; first-snapshot test files are included so deleted tests are still covered.
2254	- `shell` checks are linted for suppression patterns and best-effort scanned for existing working-tree path tokens; matching Rust test files classify as `test`, other paths as `unknown`.
2255	
2256	### 35.4 Verdict policy
2257	
2258	The verdict is intentionally heuristic:
2259	
2260	- `refuse`: the run modified `acceptance.yaml`, a compiled check contains a suppression pattern such as `|| true`, `--no-verify`, or `--exit-zero`, or a covered test/target file was deleted. Refusal writes no marker and reuses the existing non-terminal gate-failure loop.
2261	- `caveat`: a covered test or literal check target was modified or created. The marker is signed, but the caveat is visible in status and exit summaries.
2262	- `clean`: no spec edits, no suppression lint findings, and no caveat-worthy covered-file touches. Production code edits exercised by tests stay clean; editing production code is the point of a run.
2263	
2264	### 35.5 `acceptance-tamper.json` and signature binding
2265	
2266	The proof file lives at `<run-root>/proofs/acceptance-tamper.json`:
2267	
2268	```json
2269	{
2270	  "schema_version": 1,
2271	  "run_id": "...",
2272	  "verdict": "clean",
2273	  "spec_modified": false,
2274	  "lint_findings": [],
2275	  "covered_files_touched": [],
2276	  "caveats": [],
2277	  "refusal_reasons": []
2278	}
2279	```
2280	
2281	The `AcceptanceMarker` schema stays at version 1 and receives no new fields. `gate.rs::marker_signature` hashes the tamper file bytes alongside the nonce, marker fields, and check results. Missing tamper files hash as empty bytes for backward tolerance. A forged or edited tamper file invalidates marker validation, so an agent cannot erase a caveat after signing.
2282	
2283	### 35.6 Surfacing
2284	
2285	`status`, exit cards, `show --why-failed`, and attach activity derive a per-check gate line from marker/progress rows, for example `gate: PASSED 4/4` or `gate: FAILED 0/1 - cargo_test x auth::tests::expired_token`. Tamper proof data adds `tests modified this run: yes/no` and caveat text such as `accepted (caveat: agent modified test file tests/auth_test.rs this run)`. Exit cards render caveat gates with `Warn` tone.
2286	
2287	### 35.7 Honest subscription spend
2288	
2289	The same result surfaces no longer render subscription-only CLI routes as `~$0.000000`. Subscription-only spend reads `not metered (subscription) · wall <s>s · <n> turns`. Mixed routes show the metered total and append `+ subscription turns`.
2290	
2291	### 35.8 Limits
2292	
2293	This is tamper-evidence, not a causal soundness proof. It does not prove that a covered-file edit caused a pass, does not understand every language's test conventions, and does not sandbox the checks' own writes. Those larger designs are tracked in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
2294	
2295	---

2298	
2299	A **campaign** runs one large goal as N independent, separately-coordinated
2300	workstreams and composes their results into a single promoted run. The launch

GOAL: Decompose deadreckon's governance core into **composable seams**. Today `policy`, the `model-catalog`, before/after `hooks`, and the `event-sink` are compiled into the binary — changing any means forking the Rust, the framework-monolith trap the iii harness-decomposition post (Piccolo) names. deadreckon already externalizes two seams (`cli:*` providers as sandboxed subprocesses, `dr-gate` as a separate signing binary); generalize that into **one** uniform seam contract so those four become swappable from `config.toml`, the acceptance gate stays deliberately **non-swappable** (a swappable trust root is a forgeable one), and the unbounded-history gap on the direct-API path is closed. Headline word: **Composable**.

**Read first.**

- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-31-1644-deadreckon-composable-seams-rider.md` — the contract: seam primitive, per-seam wire shapes, fail policies, named depth tests.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` — §13 gate, §35 tamper-evident gate, §38 module layout.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` — `run_turn_loop`; policy/hook/compaction insertion points; history join (L775).
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/{types.rs,router.rs,cli_common.rs,registry/mod.rs,config.rs}` — `Provider`, router, subprocess contract, `ModelEntry`, config.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/{gate.rs,events.rs}` + `.../src/bin/dr-gate.rs` — the non-swappable trust root; `RunEventKind`.
- Prior riders in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/` — invariants hold.

**Posture.** Production-release track. Files-not-fields: seam wiring is a new `[seams]` table in `config.toml`; per-run audit is new files (`seams.json`, `compaction.jsonl`). No `PipelineState`/`Plan`/`AcceptanceMarker`/`ProviderEntry` schema changes. The **gate is not a seam** and never becomes one; built-in telemetry, `events.jsonl`, and `dr-gate` are untouched. No `git push`. Edits inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`. Larger designs → `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.

**One primitive.** A `SeamCommand`: run the configured external command **sandboxed**, JSON request on stdin → JSON response on stdout, enforce a timeout, apply a per-kind fail policy. No command configured ⇒ the built-in default runs, behavior identical. Installing/removing a command is the thin↔thick slider; `--no-seams` forces all built-ins.

**Seams + the gap.**

- **policy** — per tool-call `{function_id,command,working_dir}`→`{decision:allow|deny,reason?}`. Fail-closed (timeout/error ⇒ deny). The OS sandbox stays the hard floor: a seam may only narrow it, never widen it.
- **catalog** — returns `context_window`/pricing. Fail-open ⇒ built-in `ModelEntry` list.
- **hooks** — observe-only fanout of `ToolCallStarted`/`ToolCallResult`; cannot change the decision; failures non-fatal; built-in telemetry still fires.
- **event-sink** — additive mirror of the `RunEvent` stream; `events.jsonl`+broadcast stay the source of truth (attach unaffected); failures non-fatal.
- **compaction** — direct-API path only: deterministic context-window-aware history elision keyed to the catalog `context_window`, recorded in `compaction.jsonl`, never dropping the goal/acceptance spec, identical on resume. CLI providers self-manage, untouched.

**Phases.** Eleven (P1–P11) in the rider. Each: depth test first → implement → `cargo test -p <crate> && cargo fmt --check` green → conventional local commit → CHANGELOG. P1 lands the seam primitive + gate-has-no-seam guard (RED). P11 adds AS-BUILT §39, CHANGELOG, deferrals.

**Verification.**

- Every rider depth test present and passing; `cargo fmt --check`; `git diff --check`.
- Smoke (`--smoke --sandbox none`): a `deny` policy seam blocks a tool call (denial recorded, run continues); `--no-seams` restores built-in behavior identically.
- Smoke: a catalog seam overrides a model `context_window`; a malformed catalog seam falls back to built-in without blocking the run.
- Smoke: no `[seams]` key can target the gate; no seam can write/redirect the marker or read `gate/nonce`.
- Smoke: a long direct-API run compacts deterministically while keeping the goal/acceptance spec; the CLI path is never compacted.
- No edits outside the repo; no `git push`; no durable-schema changes.

**Stop when** the four seams are swappable via `[seams]`/`--no-seams` with their fail policies, the gate stays non-swappable with green trust tests, direct-API history compacts deterministically without dropping the spec, AS-BUILT §39 + CHANGELOG record it, deferrals are in V1-CANDIDATES, verification passes, and the work is committed locally.

**One primitive.** A `SeamCommand`: run the configured external command **sandboxed**, JSON request on stdin → JSON response on stdout, with a timeout and a per-kind fail policy. No command configured ⇒ the built-in default runs, behavior identical. Installing/removing one is the thin↔thick slider; `--no-seams` forces all built-ins.

**Seams + the gap.**

- **policy** — per tool-call `{function_id,command,working_dir}`→`{decision:allow|deny}`. Fail-closed (error ⇒ deny). The OS sandbox stays the hard floor: a seam may only narrow it.
- **catalog** — returns `context_window`/pricing. Fail-open ⇒ built-in `ModelEntry` list.
- **hooks** — observe-only fanout of `ToolCallStarted`/`ToolCallResult`; cannot change the decision; non-fatal; built-in telemetry still fires.

- **compaction** — direct-API path only: deterministic context-window elision keyed to catalog `context_window`, recorded in `compaction.jsonl`, never dropping the goal/acceptance spec, identical on resume. CLI providers untouched.

**Phases.** Eleven (P1–P11) in the rider. Each: depth test first → implement → `cargo test -p <crate> && cargo fmt --check` green → conventional local commit → CHANGELOG. P1 lands the primitive + gate-has-no-seam guard (RED). P11 adds AS-BUILT §39, CHANGELOG, deferrals.

# deadreckon — Composable Seams Rider (swap a worker, keep the gate)

This rider holds the prescriptive constraints for the goal at
`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-31-1644-deadreckon-composable-seams-goal.md`.
It supersedes nothing in prior riders (notably
`2026-05-28-1556-deadreckon-tamper-evident-gate-rider.md`,
`2026-05-28-1841-deadreckon-campaign-rider.md`,
`2026-05-28-2032-deadreckon-effortless-rider.md`,
`2026-05-29-1600-deadreckon-decompose-rider.md`) — their invariants still apply.
This rider adds **one uniform seam contract** that makes four compiled-in
governance concerns — `policy`, `model-catalog`, before/after `hooks`, and the
`event-sink` — swappable from `config.toml`; keeps the acceptance gate
deliberately **non-swappable**; and closes the unbounded-history gap on the
direct-API provider path with deterministic, resume-safe compaction.

**All paths absolute.** Source `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`, runtime `~/.deadreckon/`.

## The bet this lands (read before designing)

The iii harness-decomposition post (Piccolo) argues a harness is ~15 distinct
jobs and bundling them into one framework is the mistake: each job should be an
independently-swappable worker connected by **one** primitive, so "build your
own" means "swap a worker," not "fork a framework." deadreckon already proves it
can do this where it matters most: `cli:*` providers are sandboxed subprocesses
(`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_common.rs::run_cli_with_options`, spawn at
~L79) and `dr-gate` is a separate signing binary
(`crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs`). Everything else in the governance core
is compiled in: change the policy model, the model catalogue, the per-tool-call
side effects, or where events go, and you fork the Rust.

deadreckon's answer is **not** "decompose everything uniformly." It is:
**decompose at the boundaries that buy trust or reuse; keep one non-swappable
root of trust.** This rider generalizes the existing subprocess seam into a
single `SeamCommand` contract and applies it to exactly four kinds. The
acceptance gate stays out of the seam set on purpose: a swappable trust root is a
forgeable one (the whole point of §35). The slider between a thin harness (no
seams) and a thick one (all four plus compaction) becomes a `config.toml`/flag
change, never a rebuild.

## Posture (decided — do not redesign)

- **Production-release track.** Release-blocking trust behavior, not scaffolding.
- **The gate is not a seam, ever.** `SeamKind` has no gate variant; the config
  rejects `[seams.gate]`; no seam can write `<run-root>/proofs/`, read
  `<run-root>/gate/nonce`, redirect `dr-gate`, or change the inputs to
  `gate.rs::marker_signature`. This is the linchpin invariant, depth-tested in
  P1 and P8.
- **Built-in is the default and the floor.** With no `[seams]` entry for a kind,
  that kind's behavior is **byte-identical to today** (depth-tested per seam).
  The OS sandbox (`ToolSandboxPolicy`) remains the hard floor: the `policy` seam
  may only *narrow* it, never widen it.
- **Files-not-fields.** Seam wiring is a new `[seams]` table in `config.toml`;
  per-run audit is new files `<run-root>/seams.json` and
  `<run-root>/compaction.jsonl`. **No** `PipelineState`, `Plan`,
  `AcceptanceMarker`, `AcceptanceCheckResult`, or `ProviderEntry` field additions.
- **Fail policy is fixed in code per kind, not configurable.** `policy` is
  fail-closed (deny), `catalog` is fail-open (built-in), `hooks` and `event_sink`
  are fail-safe (skip, non-fatal). Changing a fail policy changes the contract.
- **Seam workers run sandboxed.** A seam subprocess is spawned through the
  existing sandbox wrapper with the `gate/` and `proofs/` subtrees denied.
- **No `git push`.** Phased local commits only.
- **No V1 invention.** Bus/WebSocket transport, a worker registry, a
  human-approval seam, LLM-backed compaction → `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
- **Edits stay inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`.**

## Data model (files, not fields)

### `config.toml` — new `[seams]` table (and `[compaction]`)

\```toml
# Each kind is optional. Absent ⇒ built-in default for that kind.
# Allowed kinds: policy | catalog | hooks | event_sink.  gate is NOT a seam.
[seams.policy]
command = ["my-policy-worker", "--rules", "policy.yaml"]  # argv; argv[0] resolved on PATH or absolute
timeout_ms = 5000

[seams.catalog]
command = ["my-catalog-worker"]
timeout_ms = 10000

[seams.hooks]
command = ["my-hook-logger"]
timeout_ms = 2000

[seams.event_sink]
command = ["my-slack-sink"]
timeout_ms = 2000

[compaction]
fraction = 0.75              # compact when est_tokens(history) > fraction * context_window
keep_recent_turns = 6        # most-recent turns kept verbatim
fallback_context_window = 200000   # used only when the catalog reports no context_window
\```

Parsed by a **new** `SeamsConfig` (do not extend `ProviderConfigFile`), with
`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on the seams map so any unknown kind — including
`gate` — is a hard error.

### `<run-root>/seams.json` — per-run resolution audit (written once at run start)

\```jsonc
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "run_id": "…",
  "resolved_at": "RFC3339",
  "no_seams": false,                  // true when --no-seams forced built-ins
  "kinds": {
    "policy":     { "source": "external", "command": "my-policy-worker", "timeout_ms": 5000, "fail_policy": "closed" },
    "catalog":    { "source": "builtin",  "fail_policy": "open" },
    "hooks":      { "source": "external", "command": "my-hook-logger",  "timeout_ms": 2000, "fail_policy": "safe" },
    "event_sink": { "source": "builtin",  "fail_policy": "safe" }
  }
}
\```

`command` records argv[0]'s basename only (no args) — audit, not re-exec.

### `<run-root>/compaction.jsonl` — append-only, one row per compaction event

\```jsonc
{ "schema_version": 1, "turn": 14, "context_window": 200000, "fraction": 0.75,
  "est_tokens_before": 161240, "est_tokens_after": 38110,
  "kept_recent_turns": 6, "elided_turns": 7, "context_window_source": "catalog" }
\```

`context_window_source` ∈ `catalog | seam | fallback`.

## The one primitive (the spec — match it in code)

New module `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/seam.rs`, re-exported from the runtime
`lib.rs`. Runtime is the home because it already owns subprocess + sandbox
dispatch; `deadreckon-core` stays adapter-free.

\```rust
pub enum SeamKind { Policy, Catalog, Hook, EventSink }   // no Gate — by construction

enum FailPolicy { Closed, Open, Safe }                   // fixed per kind, see fail_policy_for

pub enum SeamOutcome {
    Unconfigured,            // no command for this kind ⇒ caller runs built-in
    Ok(serde_json::Value),   // parsed JSON response
    Deny(String),            // policy fail-closed result
    Fallback,                // catalog fail-open ⇒ caller uses built-in
    Skipped(String),         // hook/event_sink fail-safe ⇒ caller continues
}

// One primitive every seam goes through.
pub async fn dispatch_seam(
    kind: SeamKind,
    req: &serde_json::Value,
    seams: &SeamsConfig,
    ctx: &SeamRunCtx,        // run_root, working_dir, sandbox backend
) -> SeamOutcome
\```

`dispatch_seam` contract:
1. If `seams` has no command for `kind` → `Unconfigured`.
2. Else spawn argv **sandboxed** (reuse the sandbox path used by
   `cli_common::run_cli_with_options` / `ToolSandboxPolicy::cli_provider`), with
   `<run-root>/gate/` and `<run-root>/proofs/` denied to the child.
3. Write `req` as one JSON line to the child's stdin; read stdout to EOF; enforce
   `timeout_ms`.
4. On success + valid JSON → map to `Ok`/`Deny`/`Fallback` per kind's response
   schema. On timeout / spawn error / non-zero exit / parse error → apply
   `FailPolicy`: `Closed`→`Deny`, `Open`→`Fallback`, `Safe`→`Skipped`.

`SeamsConfig` resolution (also new in `seam.rs`):
`read_seams_config(config_path, no_seams) -> SeamsConfig`. `no_seams == true`
yields an all-empty config (every kind built-in). The config path is the one
already used to build the router (thread it through `RunLoopConfig`; default
`/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`). Write `seams.json` immediately after
resolution.

## The four seams (wire shapes + insertion points)

### policy (fail-closed) — `turn_loop.rs` bash dispatch ~L439, write_file dispatch ~L565

- Built-in floor runs **first**: `bash_policy_refusal(state, command, &policy)`
  (policy from `load_tool_policy_from_sandbox_toml(state, "bash")`). If it
  refuses, the tool call is denied and the seam is **not** consulted (a seam can
  never un-refuse the floor).
- If the floor allows, call
  `dispatch_seam(Policy, json!({"function_id":"bash","command":command,"working_dir":wd}))`.
  - Request: `{ "function_id": "bash"|"write_file", "command": "<argv or path>", "working_dir": "<abs>" }`
  - Response: `{ "decision": "allow"|"deny", "reason"?: "<text>" }`
  - `Deny` → refuse this tool call through the **existing** refusal path (emit the
    denial, feed the corrective reason into history, continue the loop). `allow`/
    `Unconfigured` → proceed.

### catalog (fail-open) — resolved at run setup, injected into the router

- Before/at `ProviderRouter` construction, runtime calls
  `dispatch_seam(Catalog, json!({}))`.
  - Response: `{ "models": [ { "id", "context_window"?, "input_per_million"?, "output_per_million"?, "aliases"? } ] }`
  - Build an override keyed by `id`/alias and inject via a new
    `ProviderRouter::with_catalog_override(map)` (or a param on
    `from_config_path_with_model`). Lookups prefer the override, else fall back to
    the built-in `registry/mod.rs::ModelEntry` list (`BUILTIN_DESCRIPTOR_SOURCES`).
  - `Fallback`/malformed/timeout → built-in catalog; the run is never blocked.

### hooks (fail-safe, observe-only) — alongside event emits in `turn_loop.rs`

- After each built-in `ToolCallStarted` (bash ~L428, write_file ~L555) and
  `ToolCallResult` (bash ~L535, write_file ~L617) emit, call
  `dispatch_seam(Hook, <event-json>)`.
  - Request: the serialized `RunEventKind` value.
  - Response: ignored except for logging. The hook **cannot** change the policy
    decision and **cannot** block; `Skipped` on any failure. Built-in telemetry
    (snapshots, provenance, traces, `events.jsonl`) is untouched.

### event-sink (fail-safe, additive) — one broadcast subscriber in runtime

- `events.rs::emit_event` (core) is unchanged; `events.jsonl` + the broadcast
  sender stay the source of truth. When the `event_sink` seam is configured,
  runtime ensures a `broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>` exists and spawns **one**
  forwarder task that subscribes and pipes each event to the sink command
  (`dispatch_seam(EventSink, <event-json>)`), `Skipped` on failure. Attach is
  unaffected (it still reads the file/broadcast).

## Context-window compaction (the gap) — `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/compaction.rs`

Today `run_turn_loop` accumulates `history: Vec<String>` and sends
`history.join("\n")` (turn_loop.rs:775) to the provider every turn with **no**
bound (`http.rs::payload` passes `request.prompt` as-is). CLI providers self-manage
their own context; the **direct-API (HTTP) path does not**. Close only that gap.

- `estimate_tokens(s) -> usize` = `s.chars().count() / 4` (deterministic).
- `compact_history(history, spec_prefix_len, context_window, cfg) -> (Vec<String>, Option<CompactionRecord>)`:
  - `threshold = (context_window as f64 * cfg.fraction) as usize` tokens. If
    `estimate_tokens(joined) <= threshold` → return history unchanged, `None`.
  - Else retain (a) the **spec prefix** (the leading goal + acceptance segment of
    the prompt — never elided) and (b) the most recent `cfg.keep_recent_turns`
    turns verbatim; replace the middle with one deterministic marker:
    `[seam:compaction] elided <N> earlier turns (~<T> tokens) to fit context window <W>; full history in history.json`.
  - Deterministic: identical inputs ⇒ identical output (no time, no randomness) —
    this is the resume-safety contract.
- Wire at the history-build site (turn_loop.rs ~L154 / before the L775 join)
  **only when the run's provider kind is HTTP/API** (guard on
  `ProviderKind`); CLI subagent prompts are never compacted.
- `context_window` comes from the (possibly seam-overridden) catalog for the
  run's model; if `None`, use `cfg.fallback_context_window` and record
  `context_window_source: "fallback"`. Append a `CompactionRecord` to
  `compaction.jsonl` on every compaction.

## The non-swappable gate (the invariant)

The gate is the one place deadreckon must refuse the article's "swap any layer"
ethos. Concretely, all of the following are guaranteed and depth-tested:

- `SeamKind` has no `Gate` variant; `[seams.gate]` is a hard config error.
- Seam subprocesses are sandboxed with `<run-root>/gate/` and
  `<run-root>/proofs/` denied — a malicious seam cannot read `gate/nonce` or
  write a marker.
- No seam touches the inputs of `gate.rs::marker_signature` (nonce + marker
  fields + check results + tamper file + rollup). A clean run with all seams +
  compaction active produces an identically-bound, valid signature.

## Flag / surface signatures

\```
deadreckon run <goal>  [--no-seams]        # force built-ins for every kind this run
deadreckon start <goal> [--no-seams]       # same, through the guided path
deadreckon doctor                          # adds a "seams" section: per-kind builtin/external + timeout
\```

Refusal / surfacing cases:

| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `[seams.gate]` present | config refused: `the gate is not swappable`; no run |
| `[seams.<unknown>]` | config refused: unknown seam kind |
| `command` empty / `timeout_ms <= 0` | config refused with the offending kind named |
| `--no-seams` | `seams.json.no_seams = true`; every kind `builtin`; behavior identical to today |

## Phases (eleven)

Each phase: write the named depth test(s) **first** and watch them fail;
implement; green on `cargo test -p <touched crate>` plus `cargo fmt --check`;
conventional-commit local commit; one-line CHANGELOG entry. Do not run
`make verify` / release / stress / full-workspace suites unless the human asks.

### P1 — Seam primitive + config + per-run audit + gate-guard (RED)

- Add `seam.rs`: `SeamKind` (no `Gate`), `FailPolicy`, `SeamOutcome`,
  `SeamsConfig` with `deny_unknown_fields`, `read_seams_config`, `dispatch_seam`
  (sandboxed spawn, JSON stdio, timeout, per-kind fail policy), and `seams.json`
  writer. No seam wired into behavior yet.

Depth tests (`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/seam.rs`):
- `seam_kind_has_no_gate_variant`
- `seams_config_rejects_gate_key`
- `dispatch_unconfigured_kind_returns_unconfigured`
- `dispatch_round_trips_json_request_and_response`
- `dispatch_timeout_applies_kind_fail_policy`
- `resolution_writes_seams_json_with_sources_and_fail_policies`

### P2 — policy seam (fail-closed; sandbox stays the floor)

- Wire `dispatch_seam(Policy, …)` after the built-in floor at the bash and
  write_file dispatch points; map `Deny` to the existing refusal path.

Depth tests (`crates/deadreckon-runtime/`):
- `policy_seam_deny_blocks_tool_call_and_records_denial`
- `policy_seam_allow_proceeds`
- `policy_seam_timeout_denies_fail_closed`
- `policy_seam_cannot_widen_sandbox_floor`
- `unconfigured_policy_seam_is_identical_to_today`

### P3 — model-catalog seam (fail-open)

- Resolve at setup; inject override into the router; fall back to built-in.

Depth tests (`crates/deadreckon-providers/` + runtime setup):
- `catalog_seam_overrides_context_window_and_pricing`
- `catalog_seam_malformed_falls_back_to_builtin`
- `unconfigured_catalog_uses_builtin_model_entry_list`

### P4 — hook-fanout seam (observe-only, fail-safe)

- Fan out `ToolCallStarted`/`ToolCallResult` to the hook command; ignore its
  response; never block.

## Integration matrix

| Seam | Wire | Default (unconfigured) | Fail policy | Can affect the gate? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| policy | per tool-call allow/deny | sandbox.toml floor only | fail-closed (deny) | no |
| catalog | model list | built-in `ModelEntry` | fail-open (built-in) | no |
| hooks | tool events (observe) | none | fail-safe (skip) | no |
| event_sink | `RunEvent` mirror | `events.jsonl` + broadcast | fail-safe (skip) | no |
| compaction | history elision (API path) | none (unbounded today) | deterministic | no (never drops spec) |
| **gate** | — | `dr-gate` (built-in) | — | **n/a — not a seam** |

## Error-footer canonical pairs

| Error | `try:` |
|---|---|
| `seam 'policy' denied bash: <reason>` | `deadreckon show <id>` to review, or adjust the policy worker / re-run with `--no-seams` |
| `seam 'catalog' failed; using built-in catalog` | check `[seams.catalog].command` in config.toml; `deadreckon doctor` |
| `config error: [seams.gate] is not allowed (the gate is not swappable)` | remove `[seams.gate]`; the acceptance gate is the trust root |
| `config error: [seams.<x>] unknown seam kind` | use policy / catalog / hooks / event_sink; see `deadreckon doctor` |
| `seam 'hooks' timed out (non-fatal)` | raise `[seams.hooks].timeout_ms` or remove the hook; the run continued |

(Each footer is exercised by a P7/P9 depth test.)

## Config additions

See the `[seams]` and `[compaction]` blocks under **Data model**. Defaults when a
section is absent: every kind built-in; `fraction = 0.75`,
`keep_recent_turns = 6`, `fallback_context_window = 200000`.

## Out of scope (explicitly V1 candidates)

- **Human-in-the-loop approval seam** (`needs_approval` / pause-and-resume):
  deadreckon is unattended-first with no interactive approval surface; revisit
  with the article's approval-gate worker model.
- **Provider-backed (LLM) compaction summaries**: this milestone elides
  deterministically; semantic summarization needs cost/eval/determinism policy.
- **Persistent bus / WebSocket transport + a long-lived worker registry**: the
  contract is per-call subprocess JSON-over-stdio; a daemon/bus needs
  lifecycle/backpressure design.
- **Seam versioning, capability negotiation, a published seam registry.**
- **Routing built-in telemetry (snapshots/provenance/traces) through the hook
  seam**: today hooks are additive observers; unifying needs the durable-audit
  guarantees preserved.
- **Catalog capabilities beyond `context_window`/pricing** (vision/tools/streaming).
- **A policy seam that can widen the OS sandbox** (deliberately impossible).

## Dependencies (Tier 1 / 2 / 3 policy)

Tier 1 (already in-tree): `serde`/`serde_json` (wire + audit files), `tokio`
(subprocess + timeout, already used by the sandbox), `toml` (config), `chrono`
(timestamps). **No new crates expected.** Tier 2: none. Tier 3: same blocks as
prior riders (no network services, no DB, no bus runtime).

## Engineering invariants (do not violate)

- **No `PipelineState`/`Plan`/`AcceptanceMarker`/`AcceptanceCheckResult`/
  `ProviderEntry` field additions.** Seam config is the `[seams]` table; per-run
  state is `seams.json` / `compaction.jsonl`.
- **The gate is not a seam.** `SeamKind` has no `Gate`; `[seams.gate]` is
  refused; no seam writes `proofs/`, reads `gate/nonce`, or alters
  `marker_signature` inputs. Guarded by P1 and P8.
- **Built-in is the default and the floor.** Unconfigured kind ⇒ behavior
  identical to today (one depth test per seam). The policy seam may only narrow
  the sandbox, never widen it (`policy_seam_cannot_widen_sandbox_floor`).
- **Fail policy is fixed per kind in code** (policy=closed, catalog=open,
  hooks/sink=safe). Changing it changes the contract.
- **Seam workers run sandboxed**; a seam failure never blocks the gate or
  corrupts the audit trail.
- **Compaction determinism is the spec** (resume-safety); changing the algorithm
  changes the contract (`identical_inputs_produce_identical_compaction`).
- **One depth test before each phase implementation.** A phase whose tests were
  never red is suspect; P1 proves the primitive + gate-guard first.
- **No silent expansion.** Anything beyond P1–P11 → `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.

## Process invariants

- Phased local commits only. No `git push`.
- Each phase ends with its depth tests passing, `cargo fmt --check` clean, and a
  CHANGELOG entry naming the SHA.
- Run focused `cargo test -p <crate>` for touched crates plus `cargo fmt --check`;
  do not run full `make verify` / release / stress suites unless the human asks.
- If a phase reveals a V1-architecture decision (bus transport, approval
  surface), stop and log it in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`; do not expand scope.
- Optional after P11: a short asciinema cast of swapping the policy seam and of
  `--no-seams`, under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/` demo assets. Skip if it doesn't
  earn it.

GOAL: Decompose deadreckon's governance core into **composable seams**. Today `policy`, `model-catalog`, `hooks`, and the `event-sink` are compiled in — change any and you fork the Rust (the monolith trap iii's harness post, Piccolo, names). deadreckon already externalizes two (`cli:*` providers, `dr-gate`); generalize into **one** uniform seam contract so those four become swappable from `config.toml`, keep the gate deliberately **non-swappable** (a swappable trust root is forgeable), and close the unbounded-history gap on the direct-API path. Headline word: **Composable**.

**Read first.**

- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-31-1644-deadreckon-composable-seams-rider.md` — the contract: primitive, wire shapes, fail policies, depth tests.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` — §13 gate, §35 tamper, §38 layout.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` — `run_turn_loop`; insertion points; L775 history join.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/{types.rs,router.rs,cli_common.rs,registry/mod.rs,config.rs}` — `Provider`, router, subprocess contract, `ModelEntry`.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/{gate.rs,events.rs}` + `.../bin/dr-gate.rs` — trust root; `RunEventKind`.
- Prior riders in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/` — invariants hold.

**Posture.** Production-release track. Files-not-fields: seam wiring is a new `[seams]` table in `config.toml`; per-run audit is new files (`seams.json`, `compaction.jsonl`). No `PipelineState`/`Plan`/`AcceptanceMarker`/`ProviderEntry` schema changes. The **gate is not a seam**; built-in telemetry, `events.jsonl`, and `dr-gate` are untouched. No `git push`. Edits inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`. Larger designs → `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.

**One primitive.** A `SeamCommand`: run the configured command **sandboxed**, JSON on stdin → JSON on stdout, with a timeout and a per-kind fail policy. No command ⇒ the built-in default runs, behavior identical. Installing/removing one is the thin↔thick slider; `--no-seams` forces all built-ins.

**Seams + the gap.**

- **policy** — per tool-call `{function_id,command,working_dir}`→`{allow|deny}`, **fail-closed**; the OS sandbox stays the floor (seams only narrow it).
- **catalog** — returns `context_window`/pricing; **fail-open** ⇒ built-in `ModelEntry` list.
- **hooks** — observe-only fanout of tool events; can't change the decision; non-fatal; built-in telemetry still fires.
- **event-sink** — additive mirror of `RunEvent`; `events.jsonl` stays source of truth (attach unaffected); non-fatal.
- **compaction** — direct-API path only: deterministic context-window elision keyed to catalog `context_window`, logged to `compaction.jsonl`, never dropping the goal/acceptance spec, identical on resume.

**The judgment calls I baked in** (veto any of these):
- **"One primitive" = a sandboxed subprocess with JSON-on-stdin → JSON-on-stdout + timeout + per-kind fail policy** — *not* a WebSocket bus/daemon (deferred to V1). This is deadreckon's existing idiom (`cli:*` providers, `dr-gate`), faithful to the article's "one primitive" without importing iii's runtime.
- **Fixed per-kind fail policies**: policy = fail-closed (deny), catalog = fail-open (built-in), hooks/event-sink = fail-safe (skip). Not configurable — changing one changes the contract.
- **The gate is excluded by construction**: `SeamKind` has no `Gate`, `[seams.gate]` is a config error, and seam workers are sandboxed *out of* `gate/` and `proofs/` — so a malicious seam can't read the nonce or write a marker. The trust boundary is enforced, not just documented (P1 guard + P8 adversarial sweep).
- **The OS sandbox stays the hard floor** — a policy seam can only *narrow* it, never widen. A permissive/compromised policy worker can't grant more access than the sandbox allows.
- **Human-in-the-loop approval (`needs_approval`) is deferred to V1** — deadreckon is unattended-first and has no interactive approval surface.
- **Compaction is deterministic elision** (no LLM summary), **API-path-only**, keyed to the catalog's `context_window` (which ties the catalog seam to the gap-close), **resume-safe**, and **never drops the goal/acceptance spec**.
- **Files-not-fields throughout**: a new `[seams]` table + `seams.json`/`compaction.jsonl`; **zero** `PipelineState`/`Plan`/`AcceptanceMarker`/`ProviderEntry` schema changes.

**Grounded, not guessed**: the compaction gap is confirmed in code — `turn_loop.rs:775` joins unbounded history and `http.rs:89` sends it as-is; the only `context_window`/`truncate` symbols live in `flight.rs` telemetry.
